one_line: A WebMCP-native marketplace and shared workspace for humans and outside agents to research, organize, and negotiate interesting goods.
what_it_does: Combines marketplace listings with durable boards, agent research notebooks, comparisons, alerts, offers, and human approval boundaries.
leverage_rationale: The shared durable canvas and structured state make human-agent commerce collaboration materially different from an agent merely driving marketplace UI.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes shared durable canvas, agent findings beside marketplace objects, persistent notes, decisions, undo history, and approvals.
Transcript says outside agents re-discover a signed-in workspace and receive focused capability packs.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, unusually broad marketplace/workbench workflow with visible storyboard states, though the frame sheet is mostly marketing/storyboard evidence and does not prove every claimed flow.
execution_evidence: Video transcript gives a sequential signed-out setup, sign-in rediscovery, search/comparison, board organization, research, and approval workflow.
Frame sheet visibly shows consistent landing/content states, organization controls, and a side panel progression.
impact_rationale: It targets a real pain point for collectors and buyers whose cross-tab research, alerts, and negotiation memory are fragmented.
impact_evidence: About text identifies browsing, research, alerts, negotiation, and multi-party trade as fragmented problems.
Transcript describes concrete buyer workflows and human-controlled consequential actions.
creativity_rationale: The outside-agent, shared-canvas marketplace and structured verification boundary are a memorable, ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Product explicitly avoids embedding its own LLM and instead gives trusted outside agents a shared workspace.
Agent reasoning, cited research, and deal state persist beside marketplace objects.
usability_note: Canvas-first collaboration and visible approvals appear usable, but the broad scope may create complexity.
red_flags: Very broad claimed scope; not every feature is visibly demonstrated in the supplied frames.
advance_reason: High leverage and originality with credible product-motion evidence.

one_line: Tools to package and monetize a ChatGPT workspace for a book or seminar, including a shareable business-card-like representation.
what_it_does: The submission links ArrowGram, LastRevision.pro, and GetPaidX, but provides little concrete product description beyond monetizing and representing AI workspaces.
leverage_rationale: The packet does not establish what WebMCP changes beyond exposing a conventional publishing or monetization workflow.
leverage_evidence: About text only states it is built with WebMCP and gives external links; no tools or shared-state behavior is described.
execution_rationale: Evidence is extremely thin: no video, only two gallery images and a packaging screenshot, with no end-to-end workflow demonstrated.
execution_evidence: FACTS reports no video and only two gallery images.
About text is a short pitch with links and no functional walkthrough.
impact_rationale: Authors, seminar creators, and educators could plausibly value monetizable AI workspaces, but the fit and demonstrated value are unclear.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies books and live seminars as intended contexts.
No concrete user outcome is evidenced.
creativity_rationale: The concept has a potentially interesting packaging/monetization angle, but the packet does not provide enough detail to judge originality deeply.
creativity_evidence: Pitch combines AI workspace business cards with monetization.
usability_note: Insufficient visual and workflow evidence to assess usability.
red_flags: Multiple external products/links make scope unclear
advance_reason: Insufficient evidence of a coherent WebMCP product or completed workflow.

one_line: A leased, human-approved dispatch desk that brokers one agent across separate relief-organization origins with an auditable ledger.
what_it_does: Coordinates capacity and dispatch across independent relief sites using scoped leases, mounted tools, expiry/revocation, and approval for consequential commits.
leverage_rationale: The core product is the structured seam between independent origins: leases govern access, tools mount dynamically, and ledgered state enables reliable cross-origin coordination that UI automation cannot replicate comparably.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes seven desk verbs, lease state machine, dynamic mounting, five origins, and ledger entries including refusals.
Human approval is required before the real-world spending/commit step.
execution_rationale: The video transcript gives a clear end-to-end dispatch scenario and the frame sheet shows the product identity and a test/results state, though some frames are repetitive and low-legibility.
execution_evidence: Transcript walks from pantry capacity through leased cross-origin calls, ledgering, refusal, and approval boundary.
Frame sheet visibly shows the branded dispatch concept and a run/status panel.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete, high-stakes coordination failure in disaster relief and medical supply logistics, with human control preserved.
impact_evidence: Detailed Pakistan flood scenario identifies double promises, full shelters, and insulin visibility failures.
Product maps directly to relief organizations sharing a queue without surrendering their own records.
creativity_rationale: The lease-and-seam framing, dynamic tool surface, and refusal-inclusive ledger are a novel, deeply pursued WebMCP interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Cross-origin lease state machine is the product boundary.
Tool changes communicate invalidation and access scope rather than merely returning errors.
usability_note: The constrained seven-verb desk and color-keyed origins support understandable operations, though the security model adds conceptual overhead.
red_flags: Frame sheet is repetitive and low legibility; some visual details cannot be independently checked.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and strong evidence-backed execution for a high-stakes use case.

one_line: A career OS for discovering jobs, tailoring applications, and tracking the full job-search lifecycle with human approval before submission.
what_it_does: Unifies job discovery, fit scoring, resumes, cover letters, application capture, CRM, and interview tracking for humans and agents.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools can reduce friction across a fragmented career workflow, but the packet does not clearly show that WebMCP enables capabilities unavailable to a general agent with UI access.
leverage_evidence: About text lists agent-accessible discovery, scoring, tailoring, capture, and tracking.
Human approval is retained for application submission.
execution_rationale: The described scope is coherent and the live demo is reported alive, but there is no video and the seven gallery screenshots are not functionally inspectable here beyond packaging metadata.
execution_evidence: FACTS reports demo_alive=alive and seven gallery images.
About text describes a complete lifecycle but does not provide end-to-end motion evidence.
impact_rationale: Job seekers face exactly the fragmented workflow this product consolidates, and the approval boundary is appropriate for consequential applications.
impact_evidence: About text enumerates fragmented job boards, resumes, portals, recruiter messages, and interview notes.
Product directly addresses discovery through interview tracking.
creativity_rationale: A career OS is a useful synthesis with a human-agent safety angle, but the concept remains within a familiar productivity/CRM category.
creativity_evidence: Multi-user human/agent career OS with approval before submission.
usability_note: Unified lifecycle and approval controls suggest good usability, but visual evidence is limited.
red_flags: Large claimed scope is not demonstrated end-to-end
advance_reason: Strong audience fit and plausible product coherence, despite limited motion evidence.

one_line: A human-reviewed WebMCP readiness inspector that turns existing website interactions into testable agent-tool candidates.
what_it_does: Scans DOM, Shadow DOM, and same-origin frames; groups interactions; drafts tool metadata; and preserves developer review over meaning, authorization, and execution.
leverage_rationale: It directly addresses the hard adoption work of converting arbitrary interfaces into structured, reviewable WebMCP surfaces; this is more than a site-specific convenience layer.
leverage_evidence: About text describes reusable scanning across ecommerce, games, productivity, and finance.
It distinguishes native forms, composite workflows, imperative actions, and ignored/low-confidence elements while requiring review.
execution_rationale: The product scope and safety posture are coherent, with frame sheets submitted, but no transcript and limited evidence of a complete scan-to-test workflow.
execution_evidence: FACTS reports public repo, live demo, four gallery images, and three video frame sheets.
About text specifies DOM scanning, candidate grouping, metadata drafting, and developer review.
impact_rationale: Web developers and organizations adopting WebMCP have a clear recurring inspection/schema/authorization problem that ToolForge targets.
impact_evidence: About text frames the gap as applying across many website categories.
Human-in-the-loop review reduces risk of blindly exposing clickable elements.
creativity_rationale: The readiness-inspector approach is a strong infrastructure interpretation of WebMCP, especially its uncertainty classification and evidence-backed candidates.
creativity_evidence: Does not infer business intent blindly from DOM; it produces reviewable candidates.
Cross-site injectable inspector generalizes beyond one showcase app.
usability_note: Grouping and review workflow should help developers, though injected tooling may be technically complex.
red_flags: No transcript; end-to-end execution is claimed more than shown.
advance_reason: Strong infrastructure concept with meaningful WebMCP leverage and credible stated implementation.

one_line: A governed supplier portal where agents handle repetitive B2B finance workflows while humans approve consequential submissions.
what_it_does: Provides tools for invoice/document submission, exceptions, evidence, cases, payments, and finance-system updates in an authenticated portal.
leverage_rationale: Structured governed tools can make repetitive portal work more reliable, but the packet does not establish a transformative shared-state interaction beyond a well-tooled portal.
leverage_evidence: About text says 12 governed WebMCP tools cover supplier-finance workflows.
Human-in-the-loop review is used for submission and judgment.
execution_rationale: The authenticated portal and stated stack/demo are coherent, with frame sheets available, but there is no transcript and the end-to-end workflow is not fully evidenced.
execution_evidence: FACTS reports public repo, live demo, two gallery images, and three frame sheets.
About text identifies authenticated implementation and concrete portal operations.
impact_rationale: Supplier payment portals create real repetitive work and costly integrations; a governed agent surface could materially help finance teams and suppliers.
impact_evidence: About text identifies frustrated suppliers and repetitive manual payment work.
Concrete tasks include invoices, exceptions, evidence, cases, and payment tracking.
creativity_rationale: The B2B supplier-portal application is practical and well-targeted, but the interaction model is a familiar agent-enabled workflow.
creativity_evidence: Combines supplier portal operations with explicit approval governance.
usability_note: A focused portal and approval controls should be understandable, though authentication and finance exceptions add complexity.
red_flags: Authenticated workflow not fully demonstrated in packet
advance_reason: Credible practical impact and coherent implementation, with moderate evidence limits.

one_line: A flight-risk system for organ transport that withdraws stale recommendations when aircraft evidence changes.
what_it_does: Computes mission margin from cargo acceptance, aircraft rotation, and delivery constraints; returns signed certificates and invalidates tools when the selected plan becomes unsafe.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central to communicating live capability/state changes: stale plan tools are unregistered and toolchange informs the agent, preventing continued use of invalid recommendations.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows certificate-based plan selection and revalidation, then aircraft swap causing tool withdrawal and replan.
Invalidation is surfaced through the agent's changing tool list rather than a merely failed UI action.
execution_rationale: The transcript demonstrates a complete, specific scenario with arithmetic, certificate output, invalidation, and replanning. Frame evidence is visually dark and somewhat repetitive but confirms a coherent operational UI.
execution_evidence: Transcript provides concrete UA flights, margins, tail numbers, binding constraints, and replan route.
Frame sheet visibly shows flight cards, negative risk values, warning states, and recommendation panels.
impact_rationale: Organ transport coordinators have a specific, high-stakes need where stale flight assumptions can cost viable organs; the system directly addresses operational safety.
impact_evidence: About text gives kidney time window and concrete ORD-BOS mission.
System explicitly withdraws recommendations when aircraft rotation changes.
creativity_rationale: Treating tool registration as a live validity contract, with signed plan certificates and capability withdrawal, is an original and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Tool withdrawal and toolchange encode world-state invalidation.
Certificate includes margin, constraint, tail number, horizon, and fingerprint.
usability_note: The named binding constraint and explicit tight/broken statuses support high-stakes decisions, though the domain is inherently complex.
red_flags: Frame sheet is dark and small-text legibility is limited.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage, impact, and evidence-backed originality.

one_line: A sourcing desk where buyers and agents compare Korean food-import data, pin suppliers, and draft approval-gated enquiries.
what_it_does: Searches customs records, compares country prices, identifies suppliers/importers, supports board pinning/highlighting, and drafts a supplier request without sending it.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets the agent operate the buyer's live comparison surface, including pinning and highlighting state that a remote MCP summary cannot reproduce; it is a meaningful structured collaboration delta.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly contrasts remote-server summaries with agent operations on the visible table.
Agent calls resolve products, retrieve prices, link suppliers/importers, pin and highlight, then stop at approval.
execution_rationale: The video transcript gives a clear lookup-to-comparison-to-draft workflow with concrete data, and the frames support a consistent sourcing-desk presentation.
execution_evidence: Transcript cites mango results, 12-month prices, 125 suppliers, and 175 importers.
Frame sheet submitted and video demonstrates product, agent actions, and approval boundary.
impact_rationale: Food import buyers have a real supplier-verification and price-benchmarking problem; customs data and side-by-side comparison directly address it.
impact_evidence: About text describes manual government-portal research, cold calls, and uncertain price normality.
Product supplies official clearance records and named suppliers/importers.
creativity_rationale: The strongest novelty is not the data lookup but the agent manipulating the buyer's visual comparison state and preserving human control over sending.
creativity_evidence: Pin/highlight tools alter what is already on the user's screen.
Brazil is dimmed rather than deleted, preserving comparative context.
usability_note: Side-by-side board interaction and explicit draft approval fit the sourcing task well.
red_flags: The underlying TAAMs data product predates the challenge; WebMCP layer is the new contribution claimed.
advance_reason: Strong demonstrated agent-human workflow with meaningful leverage and audience value.

one_line: A fantasy action RPG where an external WebMCP agent becomes a visible, reversible party member in collaborative quests.
what_it_does: Shares canonical battlefield, inventory, quests, companions, and progression state with an agent that advises and issues reversible tactical commands.
leverage_rationale: A typed agent surface over the same canonical game state enables a genuine party-member collaboration rather than a separate chat assistant or brittle UI driver.
leverage_evidence: About text says React UI and WebMCP tools operate on the same deterministic WorldEngine state.
Agent can inspect live battlefield/fellowship state, recommend actions, issue reversible commands, and propose plans for approval.
execution_rationale: The architecture and game scope are coherent, and frame sheets are supplied, but no video/transcript demonstrates the full combat or quest loop end-to-end.
execution_evidence: About text specifies deterministic engine, five realms, companions, bosses, and visible activity feed.
FACTS reports live demo and three frame sheets.
impact_rationale: It addresses the real desire for social, strategic play when friends are unavailable, with entertainment and companionship as legitimate impact.
impact_evidence: About text directly identifies scripted followers and absent friends as the problem.
Agent acts as a visible party member without secretly rewriting the game.
creativity_rationale: Making an external agent a constrained, accountable RPG party member with personality, trust, motivation, and reversible tactics is highly memorable and ambitiously pursued.
creativity_evidence: Distinct companion personalities, abilities, trust levels, and motivations.
Agent collaboration is embedded in battlefield rules and visible activity feed.
usability_note: Visible activity and reversible commands are good safeguards, though RPG complexity may increase interaction load.
red_flags: No video/transcript; central gameplay completion is claimed rather than shown.
advance_reason: Distinctive interaction model and credible game architecture warrant advancement despite limited motion evidence.

one_line: A live, verifiable engineering-impact profile and SVG badge that agents can explain, compare, and evolve with a developer.
what_it_does: Aggregates engineering activity into scored dimensions, supports verification and simulation, and produces tamper-detectable badges with human-approved writes.
leverage_rationale: Agent-readable profiles, explanations, simulations, and human-approved badge updates are useful structured capabilities, but the packet does not show WebMCP fundamentally changing the underlying analytics outcome.
leverage_evidence: About text reports 19 registrations, 18 distinct tools across discovery, profiles, verification, and badge studio.
Agents propose and preview while humans approve persistence.
execution_rationale: The concept and surfaces are coherent, with four gallery images and a live URL, but no video means the end-to-end analysis-to-badge workflow is not visually demonstrated.
execution_evidence: About text describes four scoring dimensions, confidence adjustment, multi-provider inputs, SVG badge output, HMAC signatures, and simulations.
FACTS reports live demo, public repo, and four gallery images.
impact_rationale: Developers, hiring teams, and collaborators could benefit from evidence-based explanations of engineering work beyond a CV, though interpretation and adoption are uncertain.
impact_evidence: About text identifies the gap between repository activity and claims such as reliability or quality.
Badge can evolve from GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Codeberg activity and provide explanations.
creativity_rationale: Turning engineering activity into a live, explainable, verifiable badge with counterfactual simulation is a fresh synthesis with solid ambition.
creativity_evidence: Impact Profile combines delivery, quality, consistency, breadth, optional craft, archetype, trends, and confidence.
HMAC-signed verified metrics and what-if simulations extend beyond a static profile.
usability_note: Badge and explanation surfaces could be clear, but multi-source metrics and confidence adjustments may be difficult to interpret.
red_flags: Scoring validity and user comprehension are not demonstrated
advance_reason: Original developer-facing concept with credible breadth, though execution evidence is limited.
